memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Nadab and Abihu, however, died before the Lord when they made an offering with unauthorized fire before him in the Desert of Sinai. They had no sons; so only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron. - Num 3:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard verse. Two of Aaron's sons, Nadab and Abihu, died because they offered "unauthorized fire" before the Lord — worship God had not commanded. We should not soften what happened. It is sobering, and it is meant to be.

We do not know every detail of their sin, but Scripture is clear that they treated the holy things of God carelessly, doing what seemed right to them rather than what God had commanded. Their privilege as priests did not exempt them from the seriousness of God's holiness. If anything, being near to God's presence made careless worship all the more grave.

This passage teaches us that God cares deeply about how we approach Him. Worship is not something we design to suit ourselves; it is our response to who God truly is. Reverence matters.

We must sit honestly with the weight of this before we look for comfort. God is holy, and He is not to be treated casually. Yet here is the mercy of the gospel: what we could never get right on our own, Jesus has made right for us. He is our perfect High Priest, who offered Himself once for all and opened the way to God (Heb 10:19-22). Because of Him, we approach not with careless fire, but with reverent confidence, cleansed and welcomed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you approach God with genuine reverence?
- Have you ever treated worship as something to suit yourself?
- How does Christ give you confidence to come to a holy God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, forgive me for the times I have taken worship lightly. Thank You that through Jesus I can come to You cleansed and welcomed. Amen.
